A QR code printed on a pack is a promise about a URL. When the campaign page moves, the code on every label already in circulation either breaks or goes to the wrong place, and the fix is a reprint.

QRON generates Living QR codes for packaging and labels: the code on the pack stays the same, and where it points can be changed later. A campaign URL changing no longer has to mean new artwork and a new print run.

A code that can be re-pointed also raises a fair question: how does anyone know a scan wasn't tampered with? That's why QRON can issue a stored scan that carries an Ed25519 signature, so a verifier can check it. We are explicit about the boundary: the qron.space host forwards a scan and does not verify the signature itself, and an anonymous generate is not a stored signed scan.

If you manage packaging or labels, how do you handle a destination that changes after the print run?

reddit.title: How do you handle a QR destination that changes after the labels are already printed?
reddit.body:
Printed QR codes usually encode a fixed URL. If the landing page moves, the labels already out in the world break or point somewhere stale, and the only fix is a reprint.

We work on QRON, which generates Living QR codes for packaging and labels. The code stays the same and the destination it resolves to can be changed later, so a URL change doesn't force new artwork.

The obvious worry with a re-pointable code is trust, so a stored scan can carry an Ed25519 signature that a verifier can check. To be precise about the limits: the qron.space host only forwards a scan and does not verify the signature, and an anonymous generate is not a stored signed scan.

For those of you running packaging or label programs: do you use redirect services, short links you control, or just reprint? Curious what has actually held up.

https://qron.space/?utm_source=reddit&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=living-qr-reprint&utm_content=a

Disclosure: I work on this project.
